tagline: Role-based slash commands for a sprint: office hours, plan reviews, QA, ship.
bestFor: Solo builders who want review, QA, and release discipline around Claude Code
keyFeatures: A sprint of user-invoked roles: `/office-hours` writes a design doc to `~/.gstack/projects/`, then `/plan-ceo-review`, `/plan-eng-review`, `/plan-design-review`, and `/plan-devex-review` (or `/autoplan` to chain them); implementation happens in Claude Code's own plan mode; then `/review`, `/qa`, `/ship`, and `/retro`

Adjacent to SDD rather than spec-driven: the README calls it "a process" for "a virtual engineering team", and no maintained spec or task list lives in the repository (our inference from the README, docs/skills.md, and the skill list)
Optional `/spec` skill interviews you in five phases, blocks below a 7/10 quality score, and files the result as a GitHub issue; `--execute` can spawn `claude -p` in a fresh git worktree
Plan reviews hand artifacts forward: the `/office-hours` design doc feeds the plan reviews, and `/plan-eng-review` writes a test plan that `/qa` picks up
A review-readiness table prints in the session before `/ship`; Eng Review is the only required gate and `gstack-config set skip_eng_review true` disables it
`/review` dispatches specialist reviewers as subagents; `/autoplan` adds an outside review from Codex
`/qa` drives a real browser or tests CLIs and APIs and writes regression tests; `/ship` runs a coverage audit and opens the PR; `/land-and-deploy` and `/canary` cover merge and post-deploy checks
Safety skills (`/careful`, `/freeze`, `/guard`): the destructive-command check blocks through hooks on Claude Code and is advisory on most other hosts
Claude Code is the only full-support host; Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory Droid, Kiro, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, and others are listed experimental through `./setup --host <name>`
limitations: Not spec-driven in the sense this comparison uses: no in-repo living spec, no task breakdown, and no spec-to-code check; the build step is left to Claude Code's plan mode (our inference)
Large install surface: Bun 1.4.2+, binaries compiled on the machine, hooks written to the agent config, and 62 skill directories (the README says 23 tools)
The design doc, test plan, and `/spec` archive live under `~/.gstack`, outside the repository, so they are not shared through git
No worktree or parallel orchestration of its own: the "10-15 parallel sprints" in docs/why-gstack.md rely on Conductor, a separate product
Outside reviews send code to Codex or Claude Code under the user's own login and are on by default (README privacy section); telemetry is off by default
The author's productivity figures (about 810 times a 2013 pace in logical lines per day) are not independently checked here (project's claim, not tested here)
One high-profile author and 18 contributors; repository created 2026-03-11 and changing almost daily (~142K stars, ~21K forks on 2026-11-20)
Scores assessed from the repository and its docs on 2026-11-20 (commit 92c6c8a), not from hands-on use
